title: An Explicit Five-Variable Counterexample to the Generalized Vanishing Conjecture
summary: We give an explicit counterexample in five variables to the Generalized Vanishing Conjecture. The construction is motivated by the recent counterexample to the Mathieu conjecture for SU(2). In the polynomial ring C[a,b,c,d,t], set P = (t+c)(ad+bt), Q = c, and let Λ = d/dt (d/da d/dd - d/db d/dc). We prove that Λ^m(P^m) = 0 for every m >= 1, whereas for every m >= 2, Λ^m(QP^m) = (-1)^m (m!)^2 (m+1)! t, which is nonzero. Thus the Generalized Vanishing Conjecture fails in dimension 5.
